title: Evers announces $15M in tax incentives for Madison-based nuclear fusion company
excerpt: MADISON, Wis. -- Gov. Tony Evers is opening the state's pocketbooks to support a Madison-based company making strides in nuclear fusion.
content:
MADISON, Wis. -- Gov. Tony Evers is opening the state's pocketbooks to support a Madison-based company making strides in nuclear fusion.

Evers and the Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation on Wednesday announced up to $15 million in performance-based tax incentives for Realta Fusion. The funding will help the company open an $800 million corporate headquarters and research-and-development facility at the former Oscar Mayer plant in Madison.

Realta said earlier this year that the new facility will generate over 600 jobs. The incentives announced Wednesday mean that the company will receive tax credits based on how much capital it invests in the project and how many jobs it actually creates.

"Fusion energy is not only good for our planet and our power grid, but it builds on all our strengths as a state with our world-class research universities, research laboratories, and an incredible manufacturing and supply chain network supported by our highly skilled workforce," Evers said in a statement. "I can’t wait to see all the good that will come from this project."

Realta formed as a spin-off from UW-Madison experiment and the company's ties to the university run deep. Staff operate the Wisconsin HTS Axisymmetric Mirror at the UW Physical Sciences Lab in Stoughton, and much of its staff spent time studying at UW.

Moving to the Oscar Mayer plant represents Realta's next step as it works toward creating commercial-scale fusion energy.
